plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), where bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. If I bid above my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me. If I bid below my value, I risk losing profitable opportunities where the second-highest bid is between my bid and my true value. Since payment depends on the second-highest bid, not my own bid, truthful bidding maximizes my expected profit. Therefore, I should bid exactly $36, my private value.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of others' actions. If I bid above my value, I risk winning at a price higher than my value (negative profit). If I bid below my value, I risk losing profitable opportunities where the second-highest bid is between my true value and my lowered bid. Since others are also rational and will bid their true values, the Nash equilibrium is for everyone to bid truthfully. My value is $8, so I will bid exactly $8.

In a second-price auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because: if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me. If I bid lower, I risk losing an auction I could have profitably won. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) when I win, truthful bidding maximizes my expected profit. My value is $44, so I should bid exactly $44.
